The agent card. A JSON document at a well-known URL (`/.well-known/agent-card.json`) that advertises identity, skills, capabilities, and auth requirements. It is how a client discovers what an agent can do before trusting it with anything — the agent equivalent of an OpenAPI document. L200: 2. The task. The unit of work, with a lifecycle: submitted → working → (`input-required`) → completed or failed. Tasks have IDs, so a long job can be polled, resumed, or streamed rather than held open on one blocking call. L201: 3. Messages and artifacts. Conversation turns, and the outputs a task produces. L202: Transport is deliberately boring. JSON-RPC over HTTP is an ordinary POST whose JSON body names the method to run. Server-Sent Events (SSE) keeps one HTTP response open while the server appends lines to it. Ordinary infrastructure can therefore govern an A2A endpoint. L203: L204: That is what lets Chapter 5 put agentgateway in front of it, and it is why the `input-required` state matters here: an approval pause (【57†4.5. Guardrails】) is a first-class protocol state, not a hack. L205: Run the task-lifecycle and session-mapping regressions before opening a listener: L206: L207: `cd agents/python L208: uv run pytest tests/test_server.py -q L209: ` L210: ## How do you inspect the A2A contract? L211: L212: Stop reading here and fetch the card. Every field the sections below explain is one you will already have printed. L213: L214: `cd agents/python L215: mise run a2a L216: ` L217: L218: In another terminal: L219: L220: `curl -fsS http://localhost:8080/.well-known/agent-card.json | jq '{name,url,skills}' L221: ` L222: L223: Expected name: `AgentOps Agent`; the card should list incident triage and guarded remediation. L225: The card you just fetched is built by one constructor in `server.py`. L226: L227: `# simplified L228: agent_card = AgentCard( L229: name="AgentOps Agent", L230: description="Runbook-grounded incident triage and guarded remediation for the AgentOps Open Course.", L231: # a2a-sdk 1.x advertises endpoints as a list of transport interfaces, not a single url. L232: supported_interfaces=[ L233: AgentInterface( L234: url=f"{settings.a2a_protocol}://{settings.a2a_host}:{settings.a2a_port}/", L235: protocol_binding="JSONRPC", L236: ) L237: ], L238: version=version("agentops-agent"), L239: capabilities=AgentCapabilities(streaming=True), L240: default_input_modes=["text/plain"], L241: default_output_modes=["text/plain"], L242: skills=[ L243: AgentSkill( L244: id="incident-triage", L245: name="Incident triage", L246: description="Prioritize incidents using service state, logs, and deterministic severity rules.", L253: The source constructs both `AgentSkill` records inline; the excerpt shows the first. The served `agent-card.json` still exposes a top-level `url` alongside `supportedInterfaces` for client compatibility, which is why the `jq` filter above found one. L254: The interface URL is built from three separate settings in 【96†`config.py`†github.com】 that also matter operationally: L255: L256: `# simplified L257: a2a_bind_host: str = Field(default="127.0.0.1", min_length=1) L258: a2a_host: str = Field(default="localhost", min_length=1) L259: a2a_port: int = Field(default=8080, ge=1, le=65535) L260: a2a_protocol: str = Field(default="http", pattern=r"^https?$") L261: ` L262: L263: `a2a_host` (what a client dials) and `a2a_bind_host` (what the process listens on) are deliberately distinct. L264: * `main()` binds Uvicorn to `a2a_bind_host`, which defaults to loopback `127.0.0.1`. L265: * Only the container image opts into `AGENT_A2A_BIND_HOST=0.0.0.0` to accept traffic from other pods, and `tests/test_server.py` asserts the Dockerfile sets exactly that. L266: * The card, however, is always built from `a2a_host`/`a2a_protocol`/`a2a_port`, so it advertises a client-reachable service address. L267: It never advertises the listener address `0.0.0.0`, which means "every interface," not somewhere a client can call back. L268: ## How does the server preserve tasks? L269: L270: Tasks and sessions are written to a SQLite file, not held in process memory, so a restart does not lose them. `create_app()` builds an explicit runner with a `DatabaseSessionService` and an A2A `DatabaseTaskStore`, both backed by `.state/runtime.db`. L271: The durability argument is three values in 【97†`server.py`†github.com】: L272: L273: `session_service = _A2ASessionService( L274: db_url=database_url, L275: pool_size=1, L276: max_overflow=0, L277: connect_args={"timeout": 30}, L278: ) L279: # Build the App here rather than importing the module-level one, so an injected agent L280: # (tests, embedding) is governed by the same policy plugin as the shipped composition. L281: # ``app=`` is ADK's recommended Runner form; the deprecated ``agent=``/``plugins=`` pair L282: # would attach the policy to only this Runner instead of to the application. L283: runner = _SessionSerializingRunner( L284: app=build_app(selected_agent), L285: session_service=session_service, L286: ) L287: task_engine = session_service.db_engine L288: runtime = Runtime( L289: runner=runner, L290: session_service=session_service, L291: task_engine=task_engine, L292: task_store=DatabaseTaskStore(engine=task_engine), L293: ) L294: ` L295: The task store does not open its own database — `task_engine = session_service.db_engine` reuses the session service's engine, so both stores literally share one connection. `_A2ASessionService` recovers the executor's concurrent first-use get-or-create race without discarding requested state. `_SessionSerializingRunner` then queues overlapping turns for one user and session before ADK reads its detached state snapshot; other sessions remain concurrent. L296: The lifespan closes the runner and the session service that owns that engine. This is a single-process course durability model, not a horizontally scalable database design. L297: Deeper: why one connection, ever L298: L299: `pool_size=1` with `max_overflow=0` means the pool hands out exactly one connection, ever. SQLite allows a single writer, so queueing session writes and task writes behind that one connection serializes their short transactions instead of letting two independent engines race into intermittent "database is locked"; `connect_args={"timeout": 30}` lets a queued writer wait rather than fail immediately. L300: ## What bounds one A2A task? L301: L302: A networked task can run away in ways an in-process call cannot. The caller is another agent that may itself be looping, and the work is open-ended by design. Two bounds cap a single A2A task in this repository, both configurable and both with safe defaults. L303: 1. A per-task model-call ceiling. `_bounded_request` overrides whatever `max_llm_calls` ADK's converter produced with a fixed budget: L304: L305: `# simplified L306: a2a_max_llm_calls: int = Field(default=12, ge=1, le=100) L307: ` L308: Every A2A task therefore gets at most 12 model round-trips (clamped to 1–100) before ADK aborts the run, so a delegated goal cannot silently loop forever on your token budget. Change it with `AGENT_A2A_MAX_LLM_CALLS`; `tests/test_server.py` asserts the override survives even the streaming path. 1. A wall-clock drain bound. SIGTERM is the polite stop signal a runtime sends before it kills a process. L310: The lifecycle those bounds act on is small and testable: L311: L312: `stateDiagram-v2 L313: [*] --> submitted L314: submitted --> working L315: state "input-required" as input_required L316: working --> input_required: guarded action needs approval L317: input_required --> working: confirmed with rationale L318: working --> completed: final true L319: working --> failed: final true, adk_error_code L320: completed --> [*] L321: failed --> [*] L322: note right of working L326: `test_a2a_confirmation_response_resumes_the_guarded_action_with_audit_identity` drives the left path end to end: L327: L328: 1. The task pauses at `input-required`, carrying an `adk_request_confirmation` call. L329: 2. The client resumes the same `taskId`/`contextId` with a `confirmed` DataPart — one structured JSON chunk of an A2A message — and a rationale. L330: 3. The task reaches `completed` with an attributable audit row. L331: That pause is `final: false` in a2a-sdk 1.x. The response ends there; the task does not, because the same task resumes. The `failed` edge is exercised by the stream-interruption test discussed below. L332: L333: Deeper: what the approval looks like on the wire L334: On the wire, that resume is a single `FunctionResponse` `DataPart` posted on the same task — it echoes the paused call's `id` and carries the rationale the agent requires: L335: L336: `{ L337: "kind": "data", L338: "data": { L339: "id": "", L340: "name": "adk_request_confirmation", L341: "response": { "confirmed": true, "payload": { "rationale": "runbook-backed; INC-002 verified" } } L342: } L343: } L344: ` L345: That is exactly what 【98†`clients/web/index.html`†github.com】 sends when you approve, keeping `contextId` for the session and `taskId` for the paused task. The agent refuses an approval carrying no rationale (【57†4.5. Guardrails】), which is why the browser form makes the field required. L346: The state machine above is what the server tracks; the two-request handshake below is what a client actually implements. Approval is a second `message/send` that reuses the same identifiers: L347: L348: `sequenceDiagram L349: participant C as A2A client L350: participant S as A2A server L351: C->>S: message/send (new task) L352: S-->>C: working, then input-required (final:false)
+ adk_request_confirmation L353: Note over C: user approves with a rationale L354: C->>S: message/send — FunctionResponse DataPart
same taskId + contextId L355: S-->>C: working → completed + attributable audit row` L356: A missing rationale, or a resume on a fresh `taskId`, does not continue the paused action — the guarded write only fires when the confirmation is tied back to the exact task that requested it. L357: ## How do I stream a response through the gateway? L358: L359: Call `message/stream` instead of `message/send`. The response is an SSE channel: every `data:` line is one JSON-RPC response carrying a whole task event (`submitted`, `working`, `completed`, `failed`). L360: L361: The command below is a Chapter 5 preview L362: Nothing listens on `127.0.0.1:3001` until agentgateway is up, so running this now cannot connect. The JSON-RPC body is the part that works today: send the same payload to the address the card advertises, `http://localhost:8080/`, with `mise run a2a` and a model backend running. L480: * Assuming auth is built into the A2A path. The default unauthenticated adapter derives a synthetic caller id, so a guarded write's audit row proves confirmation continuity, not real-world identity. A shared or production deployment must authenticate the caller at the gateway (【100†5.5. Gateway Security】) and propagate a durable subject before this path carries human-level accountability. L481: ## How would you write a minimal A2A client? L482: L483: Exercise: go past `curl` and script the full task-vs-session handshake yourself, so the difference between a `contextId` and a `taskId` becomes concrete rather than described. L484: * Mode: `temporary experiment`. L485: * Goal: from a short script, discover the agent, submit a guarded request, handle the approval pause, and resume it on the same task — the exact flow the reference 【98†`clients/web`†github.com】 browser client implements, reduced to its essentials. L486: * Files to touch: `.agents/tmp/a2a-handshake.py` only; the live request writes disposable runtime state under `agents/python/.state`. L487: * Preflight: require `test ! -e .agents/tmp/a2a-handshake.py`, `mise run doctor:gateway` passing, and the documented A2A plus gateway processes already running. L488: * Steps to implement: (1) `GET /.well-known/agent-card.json` through the `:3001` gateway listener and read whether the card advertises streaming; (2) send `restart_service(...)` for a down service with `message/send`, keeping the returned `contextId`; (3) observe the task settle in `input-required` rather than completing; (4) resume by sending the approval on the same `taskId`, and confirm the audit row names the approver (【101†3.1. Tools】). L489: * Gate that proves completion: the second (resume) request must reuse the `taskId` from step 2 — a new task id means you started a fresh conversation instead of answering the pending approval, which is the one mistake this exercise exists to catch. Read `clients/web/index.html` (it comments exactly when `taskId` is set and cleared) to check your handling against the reference. L490: * Final state: stop only the processes you started, run `rm -- .agents/tmp/a2a-handshake.py`, then `cd agents/python && mise run data:reset`; the script is absent and the disposable state matches the seed again. L491: ## What proves this page worked? L492: L493: `cd agents/python L494: uv run pytest tests/test_server.py tests/test_delegation.py L495: ` L496: L497: Verify card fields, advertised address, persistent service/task construction, cancellation, and shutdown cleanup. The same run covers the coordinator's sub-agent wiring and the real `input-required` confirmation response resuming the same task with attributable audit evidence. Deterministic fake models drive cancellation and approval, so no live model call is needed. L498: The focused server test should finish without a network service left behind. Apply the complete `mise run test` coverage gate at chapter exit. L499: L500: After inspecting the card, return to the terminal running `mise run a2a` and press `Ctrl-C`. The later gateway lab starts it again with the configuration that lab owns. L501: L502: You are done when: L503: * `mise run a2a` served a card whose `name` is `AgentOps Agent`, then stopped cleanly with `Ctrl-C`. L504: * `uv run pytest tests/test_server.py tests/test_delegation.py` passes. L505: * You can say which identifier carries the session (`contextId`) and which one resumes a paused task (`taskId`). L506: * You can cancel a working task and observe a terminal `canceled` state. L507: * You can name one boundary — team, release cadence, scaling, trust, or language — that would justify moving an in-process sub-agent behind A2A. L508: Continue to 【49†3.7.
